newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle trade thin $67-feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle trade thin $67-feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle on Friday traded in light volume at $67.00 per cwt, steady with active sales the previous day, feedlot sources said.
About 3,000 head sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma after a weekly movement of 102,500, they said.

In Kansas, about 200 head (100 each of slaughter steers and heifers) sold at $67.00 following weekly sales of 71,300, including 13,700, or about 19 percent, previously contracted or formulated cattle.
Brisk sales this week in the Panhandle depleted the estimated show list of 95,000 head, feedlot sources said.
A moderate number of this week's estimated show list of 86,000 head in Kansas reportedly were sold, which was expected to leave some cattle carried over to next week, the feedlot sources said.
Some of the cattle carried over were said to be unfinished and could use a few extra days on feed to reach desirable market weights, they said.
Weather was expected to be mild during the weekend, which should not hinder cattle weight gains, the sources said.
